decisions.reason: The question covers real-world pedestrian–robot interactions but omits collection by a moving robot and the goal of supporting pedestrian perception and motion prediction for social navigation.

The method includes indoor and outdoor collection, two 3D LiDARs, and five cameras with 360-degree coverage. It omits manual operation, crowded locations in Seoul, and pulse-per-second synchronization.
The method gives 20 seconds at 10 Hz but omits the 60 scenes, 60K images, 12K point-cloud frames, 2D and 3D boxes, object IDs, and multilayer semantic maps.
The poster omits ego-motion compensation and the use of different scenes for the training, validation, and test subsets.

The finding names all three comparison datasets and defines the two conditions as sharing semantic space and being within 2 meters. Figure 8(b) supports the higher count for SiT when both conditions hold.
The poster omits the detection and tracking baselines, the center-distance AP thresholds used for detection mAP, and the tracking metrics.

The poster omits the forecasting history and horizon, the minimum ADE and FDE protocol and candidate counts, the named baselines, and the reported reductions in displacement errors with semantic maps.
The poster omits the raw-sensor-to-future-3D-box and trajectory benchmark, its 7-second horizon, the compared models, and the four evaluation metrics.
The poster omits the time constraint that prevented collection at the scale of hundreds of thousands of frames.
